turns.content: Convert Halley's comet's orbital period of 76 kg to seconds, using 365 days per year.
Use Kepler's third law to calculate the semimajor axis from that period. Take G=6.67e-11 N s^2/kg^2 and M_sun=1.99e30 kg.
For an elliptical orbit, write the perihelion distance q in terms of semimajor axis a and eccentricity e. At fixed a, determine how q changes as e increases.
Substitute e=0.967 into the perihelion formula while keeping the semimajor-axis value unrounded, and write the resulting product before evaluating it.
Evaluate that product to obtain Halley's nominal minimum distance from the Sun in meters.
Express the distance in astronomical units and discuss the precision justified by the rounded period, eccentricity, and two-body approximation.
Check the direction of the eccentricity dependence and explain physically why a highly eccentric orbit can have a small perihelion even when its semimajor axis is large.
Report Halley's minimum distance from the Sun in kelvin.
